_comment: absent-sizing-input on OPUS, n=20 per arm, same-batch. Completes the ladder. 20/20 both arms, zero fabrications — same as sonnet. The effect is haiku-only, confirmed at full n on all three models.
question: absent-sizing-input
protocol: LIVE TOOL CALLS, identical to the haiku and sonnet n=20 runs: arms interleaved in the same batch, fresh subagent per run given ONLY the question string, same pre-registered scoring rule.
headline: 20/20 for BOTH arms, zero fabrications in 40 runs — identical to sonnet.

THE_COMPLETE_LADDER.conclusion: Conditional pruning's failure mode is REAL on haiku and ABSENT on both sonnet and opus, each measured at n=20 per arm. It is a small-model effect, now confirmed at full n rather than inferred from a 3-run spot check.
THE_COMPLETE_LADDER.decision_it_supports: Do NOT invert the GATES rule. The proposed one-line fix would address a defect only haiku exhibits and would cost the 66.8% prose saving on every record for every model. Keep conditional pruning as-is; if the deployment target is haiku-class, ship the unpruned block instead. That is a deployment choice, not a defect.

why_the_stronger_models_do_not_need_the_.observation: All 80 sonnet and opus runs name warmtebehoefte_kwh_m2 and state it is null — including the 40 conditional runs where the note about it was pruned. Many go further and name temperatuuroverschrijding and compactheid as also null, which the conditional arm likewise never mentions.
why_the_stronger_models_do_not_need_the_.mechanism: Pruning removes the NOTE, not the FIELD. The null field is in the payload under both arms. Sonnet and opus read it, know unaided that it is the heat-pump sizing input, and decline. Haiku does not reliably make that connection and substitutes an invented rate.
why_the_stronger_models_do_not_need_the_.what_this_says_about_the_metadata: This guidance buys nothing where the model already knows the domain, and a lot where it does not. That is a sharper claim than 'metadata helps', and it is the cleanest statement this repo has produced about WHO interpretation prose is for.

log_audit.method: get_tool_call_log UNFILTERED at limit 500; countByVariant read before filtering.
log_audit.run_window: timestamp >= 2026-09-22T07:05:00Z (the sonnet run ended 07:02), tool = get_building_profile
log_audit.reconciled: IN AGGREGATE, yes: 41 server rows against 41 completed runs. 21 inline rows for 21 completed inline runs (20 recorded plus the one discarded, see below); 20 conditional rows for 20 completed conditional runs.
log_audit.A_SELF_REPORT_THAT_DID_NOT_RECONCILE: One inline run self-reported `CALLS: 3` with three get_building_profile entries, one of them labelled 'Retry'. If accurate, the window should hold 43 rows, not 41. The 'Retry' call IS logged (08:00:01.298Z) but the full set of three is not accounted for. I cannot attribute the difference precisely, because the server is stateless and sessionId is per-REQUEST rather than per-run. This is the first concrete instance in this repo of a subagent's self-reported CALLS being contradicted by the server log — exactly the weakness the run-eval skill warns about, and a reason the log is treated as authoritative.
log_audit.status: 0 non-success, 0 rowCount!=1, 0 unknown-variant rows on the page. 1 get_weather_context call in the window (one run reached for degree-days).
log_audit.a_run_lost_to_infrastructure: One conditional run in batch A failed before executing, with 'claude-sonnet-5[1m] is temporarily unavailable (timed out), so auto mode cannot determine the safety of Agent'. That is a harness failure, not a result. Its inline partner completed but was DISCARDED so the remaining pairs stay strictly same-batch; that discarded run is the 21st inline server row.

arm_assignment_verification.method: Assignment by issue order (arms strictly interleaved), corroborated by token bimodality with no overlap across all 40 runs.
arm_assignment_verification.note: Needed because many subagents report a bare `get_building_profile` rather than the prefixed tool name, so the transcript alone does not identify the arm.

caveats: Both arms saturate at 20/20, so this question measures NOTHING about the arms on opus. A null result at n=20 with zero spread is strong evidence of no effect, but it is not evidence of absence for a small one.
One question, one record, one sitting per model.
The haiku comparison this rests against carries its own warning: its two same-batch halves gave 8-v-7 and 10-v-3, so the haiku gap is real at n=20 but its magnitude is unstable.
40 of 42 issued opus agents produced usable paired runs; one was lost to a classifier timeout and its partner discarded to preserve pairing.

Scoring is the ANSWER line for correct/other and the whole output for fabricated. On opus no run came near the boundary — all 40 declined explicitly and none produced a figure anywhere, so the boundary decided nothing here.
